items.title: 56706_Buddy Tate oral history interview
items.q: So he says his wife says, 'You ever listen to Duke? ... He says, 'Oh, no, I'm with Fletcher Henderson, man.' ... So he went and told Smack. I says, 'Smack, if you get a chance, come sit down in the car with me and listen.'

ctx.x: They'd learn them solos and they was playing in those keys. Nobody could play like that and that's why the band sounds so brilliant and crisp.

Then I'll tell you what Hawk told me one time. He says, -- they were playing down on Broadway and Duke was playing uptown. So, you know, wherever Duke landed, he couldn't -- Fletcher would cut him all to pieces, they tell me, you know, he wasn't popular and things like that. So Fletcher got all the credit, you know. So he said, they were playing, they weren't even listening to anybody, you know, Fletcher got a little chesty, I guess, he said they wouldn't even listen to anybody. He said he'd go home at night and…
